title: Level outline
description: One level of a process, written by the process-level-writer agent from a brief: per step what happens, why, the outcome that proves it is done, what it uses, who does it, and what comes next. Every process reader that works one level at a time (map-process-from-data-model, map-agent-as-process) uses this format; its build script turns the outlines of every level into one business-architecture model. Step ids only need to be unique within the outline; the build makes them unique across the model.

level.description: 'top' for the top level, otherwise the id of the item (a capability, an area or a package stage) whose box this level drills down from. Matches the brief's level.

title.description: Optional title for the level. The top level's becomes the map name when the scope gives none.

source.description: Where the outline comes from when no writer wrote it: 'record-type-split' (prepare_briefs.py writes the split by record type), 'org-to-process' (taken over from an Elements org-to-process map). Left out for a writer's outline.

starts.description: What starts the level. On a child level, copy each of the parent box's input labels from the brief exactly, so the drill-down matches its box; add any other trigger the source shows as its own start.

ends.description: How the level ends. On a child level, copy each of the parent box's output labels from the brief exactly.

about.description: A step id, or an id from the brief's uses (an object apiName, a component id).

label.description: A distinct, verifiable outcome written as a completed state, naming the record or status change that proves it where there is one.

name.description: A job title or team people recognise: 'Warranty manager', 'Claims processor', 'Customer'.

kind.description: human (the default), system for an application doing the step on its own, ai-agent for an AI agent.

rasci.description: Any of R, A, S, C, I; human roles only.

name.description: The box text: an active verb and its object, sentence case, 2 to 6 words.

what.description: What happens in this step, in one or two sentences.

why.description: Why the business does it: what would go wrong without it.

roles.description: Who does it, the responsible person or team first. A reader may add further resources from the step's uses.

uses.description: Ids from the brief of what the step creates, reads, updates or runs: object apiNames from a data-model brief, component ids from an agent-package brief. The reader's build script turns them into resources on the box.

item.description: On an overview level (the top level, an area level): the id of the brief item this box stands for (a capability, an area, a package stage). When that item has a level of its own, the box drills down to it.

links.description: Help or documentation pages for the step.

next.description: The lines out of this step to other steps on this level, each labelled with the outcome that starts the next step. List the expected outcome first: the drawing puts it on the main path. Several entries with different outcomes make a decision; entries with the same outcome start those steps in parallel.

join.description: all: the step may start only when every line into it has arrived. Left out (any): any one incoming line starts it.

inferred.description: true when the source gives nothing to support this step. Do not set it on every step; the brief's rules say when.

value.description: On a level built on a lifecycle (brief cover.lifecycle): the lifecycle value this step's work puts the record in, spelt as the brief spells it. Every value has exactly one step; the step's first line out (or its end) carries the outcome and sets that value.

trigger.description: What starts the level, written as a completed state: 'Opportunity moved to Proposal'. On a child level, a parent input label copied exactly.

outcome.description: The state the level ends in. On a child level, a parent output label copied exactly.

sets.description: The lifecycle value a record has once this outcome holds, when the outcome is a status or stage change: the object's apiName and one of the values of its lifecycle in the brief, exactly as the brief spells it. The outcome label names the value too.
